message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command to bring up the Docker Engine itself – it’s the command you use to start an *existing* container. To get the Docker daemon running on a Windows machine you have a couple of options: | What you want | How to do it | |---------------|--------------| | **Start the Docker Desktop GUI** | Just double‑click the Docker Desktop icon (or run `& 'C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe'`). Once the icon turns green the daemon is ready. | | **Start the Docker service from PowerShell** | ```powershell
Start-Service Docker
``` | | **Start the Docker service from CMD** | ```cmd
net start Docker
``` | | **Start the Docker service from a one‑liner (PowerShell)** | ```powershell -Command "Start-Service Docker"``` | | **Start the Docker service from a one‑liner (CMD)** | ```cmd /c "sc start Docker"``` | > **Tip:** > • You’ll need administrative privileges to start/stop the service. > • If you’re using Docker Toolbox (the legacy “Docker Machine” setup), you’d instead run `docker-machine start default`. Once the service is running you can verify it with: ```powershell Get-Service Docker ``` or ```cmd sc query Docker ``` If you see `STATE : 4 RUNNING`, the Docker daemon is up and you can now run `docker ps`, `docker pull …`, etc.
